idiom_name: frozen { type, ... } descriptors + run() switch/handler map
implementation_notes: The algebra is a set of frozen plain objects with a literal `type` tag and pure creators (`const get = key => Object.freeze({ type: 'Get', key })`); the interpreter is a function switching on `op.type` (or a handler map). Because the values are JSON, programs can be logged, stored, sent to a worker and compared with `deepEqual` in tests - the redux-saga documentation makes exactly this the testability argument. Promises and `async/await` are the opposite: calling an async function inside a creator executes the effect immediately, so real I/O stays inside interpreter implementations. Keep a throwing default arm, since JavaScript has no exhaustiveness and a typo in `type` is otherwise a silent no-op.
pitfalls: Calling an async function inside a creator performs the effect immediately - `Get(await api.fetch(url))` is not data; pass the arguments (or a thunk) instead.
Tags are bare strings: a typo becomes a runtime failure, and without TypeScript/JSDoc union types nothing checks the algebra.
Unfrozen objects let any consumer mutate a program that is shared with a logger, cache or worker.

variants.name: Generators yielding effect descriptors, interpreted by a runtime or middleware
variants.idiom_name: function* program yielding call/take/put descriptors (redux-saga style)
variants.implementation_notes: A generator keeps the program's control flow in ordinary synchronous-looking code while every effect is yielded as a descriptor; the runtime (redux-saga middleware, an effect interpreter, a test harness) resumes the generator with the interpreter's result. This is the ergonomic high point of the pattern in JavaScript: `yield call(api.fetch, url)` reads like a call, the test is `assert.deepEqual(iterator.next().value, call(api.fetch, url))`, and no mocks are needed. Choose it where an interpreter runtime exists or is cheap to write; plain descriptor objects win when the program must be a first-class value that can be stored, reordered or serialized.
pitfalls: Yielded descriptors are only data if the effect creators are pure - `yield api.fetch(url)` yields a promise and executes the request.
Generators are single-shot state machines: a program value cannot be restarted or inspected twice, unlike an array of descriptors.
Tests must walk the generator step by step and assert `done`; an unfinished generator hides unexecuted steps.
